items.briefing:
Scammers are now using calendar invitation files (.ics) to deliver phishing attacks — meaning a seemingly harmless meeting request in your inbox could be an attempt to steal your credentials or install malware. Staff should be cautious about accepting calendar invites from unknown senders, especially if the invite contains links or asks you to log in somewhere.

In other news, a Canadian man has pleaded guilty over extortion attacks targeting organisations using the Snowflake cloud platform — a reminder that third-party cloud services can be exploited to access your data. **Practical tip:** Before accepting any calendar invite from an unfamiliar sender, check with your IT team rather than clicking links inside it.
